In the [[Mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[topology]], a '''sphere bundle''' is a [[fiber bundle]] in which the fibers are [[sphere]]s <math>S^n</math> of some dimension ''n''.<ref name="Hatcher2002">{{cite book|last=Hatcher|first=Allen|authorlink=Allen Hatcher|title=Algebraic Topology|date=2002|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9780521795401|page=442|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BjKs86kosqgC&dq=sphere+bundle&pg=PA442|accessdate=28 February 2018|language=en}}</ref> Similarly, in a disk bundle, the fibers are [[disk (mathematics)|disk]]s <math>D^n</math>. From a topological perspective, there is no difference between sphere bundles and disk bundles: this is a consequence of the [[Alexander trick]], which implies <math>\operatorname{BTop}(D^{n+1}) \simeq \operatorname{BTop}(S^n).</math>

An example of a sphere bundle is the torus, which is [[Orientability|orientable]] and has <math>S^1</math> fibers over an <math>S^1</math> base space. The non-orientable [[Klein bottle]] also has <math>S^1</math> fibers over an <math>S^1</math> base space, but has a twist that produces a reversal of orientation as one follows the loop around the base space.<ref name="Hatcher2002" />

A [[circle bundle]] is a special case of a sphere bundle.

== Orientation of a sphere bundle ==

A sphere bundle that is a product space is orientable, as is any sphere bundle over a simply connected space.<ref name="Hatcher2002" />

If ''E'' be a real vector bundle on a space ''X'' and if ''E'' is given an [[orientation of a vector bundle|orientation]], then a sphere bundle formed from ''E'', Sph(''E''), inherits the orientation of ''E''.

== Spherical fibration ==
A '''spherical fibration''', a generalization of the concept of a sphere bundle, is a [[fibration]] whose fibers are [[homotopy equivalent]] to spheres. For example, the fibration
:<math>\operatorname{BTop}(\mathbb{R}^n) \to \operatorname{BTop}(S^n)</math>
has fibers homotopy equivalent to ''S''<sup>''n''</sup>.<ref>Since, writing <math>X^+</math> for the [[Alexandroff extension|one-point compactification]] of <math>X</math>, the [[homotopy fiber]] of <math>\operatorname{BTop}(X) \to \operatorname{BTop}(X^+)</math> is <math>\operatorname{Top}(X^+)/\operatorname{Top}(X) \simeq X^+</math>.</ref>
